headline: Bone reads force
punch: And cartilage has a dedicated receptor for sensing it.

headline: Mechanotransduction
body: Chondrocytes sense mechanical load through a three tiered system: ion channels at the membrane, then intracellular signalling, then gene expression changes. Force gets converted into transcription.
punch: Load goes in one end. Gene activity comes out the other.

headline: The surprising part
body: Estrogen receptor alpha works as a ligand independent mechanotransducer in chondrocytes. It senses force with no estrogen bound to it at all, a job completely separate from its hormone role.
punch: The estrogen receptor moonlights as a strain gauge.

headline: Load in the right range
body: Appropriate mechanical loading maintains ERa expression, which keeps chondrogenic genes like COL2 and SOX9 running. SOX9 is the master transcription factor for chondrocyte identity.
punch: Loading tells the cell to keep being cartilage.

headline: Load above that range
body: Excessive or damaging loading inhibits ERa expression. COL2 and SOX9 get downregulated, while MMP13 and ADAMTS4 get upregulated. Those two are cartilage degrading enzymes.
punch: Same tissue, same receptor, opposite outcome.

headline: Which means loading
body: It isn't more equals better. There's a window where force builds and a level above it where the identical tissue starts breaking itself down instead.
punch: The variable is magnitude, not whether you load at all.

headline: The jaw specifically
body: Mandibular condylar cartilage growth responds to functional and mechanical loading, through cAMP and calcium second messenger signalling. The condyle is a growth site that reads force.
punch: Chewing load is a real input to jaw growth.

headline: And exercise loading
body: Blocking the P2Y2 purinergic receptor increased periosteal bone formation in response to exercise loading in adult mice. Adult bone still responds to load.
punch: Adult skeletons are not finished responding.

headline: So the question
body: It does, through named receptors and measurable gene changes. The question is where your loading sits on the dose response curve, because both sides of that curve are real.
punch: Build or degrade. Same mechanism decides.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
